page: Microsoft Azure E8ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a 307 GB SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU execution, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25 percent. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and cryptography operations fall within the average range. Memory performance shows a distinct contrast; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 515.05 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths are weaker, measuring 38.15 GB/sec and 22.67 GB/sec respectively. Large-model LLM inference is limited, though small-model text generation remains average at 214.75 tokens per second.

Given its high memory density and dedicated AMD EPYC cores, the E8ads_v5 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel GPU acceleration. The inclusion of a 307 GB local SSD provides a fast temporary storage tier, making it suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data buffering, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio.
